summary.intent: Advance milestone v1.1 to completion: backfill missing planning artifacts, implement the share itemName lazy-backfill endpoint (Phase 48 REQ-4 gap), ship the PR, then investigate and fix a repeatable decrypt-after-move bug discovered on staging.
summary.outcome: PR #505 shipped and merged to main (tags @cipherbox/api-v0.40.0, @cipherbox/web-v0.44.0); the PATCH /shares/:shareId/item-name endpoint is live with full client wiring and CI-passing web-e2e coverage; the decrypt-after-move root cause was fixed in both moveItem and restoreFromBin, with the BinEntry schema robustly capturing the encrypting folderKey at delete time.

repo: The GSD resume-incomplete-phase invariant produces false positives when a phase ships via PR but SUMMARY.md files are never written — always cross-check against git history and VERIFICATION.md before mechanically routing to re-execute.

backfillSentShareItemNames fires only via the SDK getCoveringShares callback on an owner file upload; ShareDialog bypasses fetchAllSentShares entirely, calling sharesControllerGetSentShares directly — no 'sent shares list' UI page triggers the backfill.

FileMetadata IPNS records are AES-256-GCM encrypted with the parent folder's folderKey at upload time; moveItem and restoreFromBin both failed to re-encrypt when reparenting, causing CryptoError: Decryption failed on any subsequent preview/download.

No move operation exists in the shared-write path (shared-write.ts exports only upload/createSubfolder/rename/delete/update/permission); within-share move is an unbuilt feature gap, not a broken path.
Batch moves route per-item through client.moveItem; folder moves are safe because a moved folder's children stay encrypted under the subfolder's own folderKey which travels unchanged.

restoreFromBin only carries originalParentIpnsName on the BinEntry — no folderKey — so restore to a different folder or after the original parent is deleted cannot re-encrypt without the new originalFolderKeyEncrypted field captured at delete time.
The release bot pushes a chore(release) commit to the PR branch immediately after gh pr create; always fetch+rebase before the final STATE push.
web-e2e only runs on main-push or manual dispatch — not on PRs — so new specs gate post-merge, not during PR review.
The web-e2e CI run uses the HTML reporter; per-test names do not appear in stdout logs, only the aggregate count (188 passed) is greppable.
The API watch-mode server auto-reloads code changes; a 401 (not 404) on a new route confirms the endpoint is live without restarting.

verify-filepointer.mjs is hardcoded to decrypt from root with rootFolderKey; it cannot verify files moved into subfolders without extending it to unwrap child folderKeyEncrypted via the vault keypair.

code.finding: moveItem re-encrypt block: guarded by `if (movedItem.type === 'file')`, resolves FileMetadata with source.folderKey, re-publishes with dest.folderKey + createVersion:false, runs inside withOperation before either folder publish so any failure aborts the move with no partial corruption.
filePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted is typed string | undefined — vitest (esbuild) masked this; tsc caught it as a latent error. A missing-key guard must be added before passing to hexToBytes.
getCoveringShares is called unconditionally before the length check in reWrapNewItems, meaning every uploadFile triggers the backfill over all sent shares.

restoreFromBin re-inserts FilePointer and publishes folder metadata but never calls resolveFileMetadata/updateFileMetadata — FileMetadata stays AES-GCM-encrypted under the original parent's folderKey, causing identical Decryption failed on restore to a different folder.
CodeRabbit finding: transient plaintext itemName bytes from TextEncoder().encode() were never zeroed after wrapping. Fixed with try/finally + fill(0) on both plaintext and ciphertext buffers.
The web createShare() always sends itemNameEncrypted — the only way to seed a legacy NULL row is by bypassing the web layer and POSTing /shares directly with the field omitted.
backfillSentShareItemNames runs as fire-and-forget (void); callers must poll GET /shares/sent for itemNameEncrypted transitioning null→hex to detect completion.
itemNameEncrypted is @IsOptional — the service stores NULL when omitted, making legacy-row seeding possible via direct API call without the web layer.

BinEntry had no folderKey field; added originalFolderKeyEncrypted (optional, for legacy compatibility) captured at deleteToBin time so restoreFromBin can re-encrypt to any target even when the original parent folder is subsequently deleted.

workflow: Sandboxed Bash cannot reach the 1Password op-ssh-sign binary — commits made inside the sandbox are silently unsigned; always use an unsandboxed shell for signed commits on repos that enforce signatures.
git rebase alone does not apply gpgsign even with commit.gpgsign=true; explicit -S flag per-pick is required (or git rebase -x 'git commit --amend -S --no-edit').
Use git cat-file -p HEAD to confirm a gpgsig header exists in the commit object — local signature verification can fail (missing allowedSignersFile) while the signature itself is valid.

Spawning a multi-agent workflow to empirically audit test harness capabilities (two-party identity, legacy-row seeding, backfill trigger, at-rest assertion) is more reliable than reasoning about it from memory — the workflow corrected several false 'human-only' assumptions.
Rebuild SDK dist before running web e2e tests when the SDK source changed — the web app consumes the built dist, not source, so stale dist silently tests old behavior.
When adding a new API endpoint, always run pnpm api:generate and commit the generated client alongside the source changes to satisfy pre-commit check-api-client.sh hooks.

friction: 1Password SSH signer wedged twice during the session — first silently produced unsigned commits (sandbox limitation), then hung with 'failed to fill whole buffer' (rc=128); required a full 1Password app restart each time.
GSD roadmap.analyze returned empty plan counts, forcing a manual directory scan to check the resume-incomplete-phase invariant.

Phase 47's false-positive resume gate (5 plans / 0 summaries, phase actually shipped) required manual git-history verification before overriding the mechanical route — the system has no affordance for 'plans shipped without summaries'.
The release bot pushes to the PR branch after gh pr create, requiring an unplanned fetch+rebase+re-sign cycle before each STATE push.
web-e2e CI HTML reporter suppresses per-test names from stdout — confirming the specific new spec ran required inferring from the aggregate test count increasing from 181 to 188.
vitest uses esbuild (no full type checking), masking the filePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted optional-string tsc error until a separate tsc --noEmit run.
Background signed commit timed out (rc=124) during a 1Password hang — had to re-stage and retry after diagnosing no lock file or hung process.
open_items: Within-share move is an unbuilt feature gap — when implemented it must re-encrypt FileMetadata to the destination subfolder folderKey (todo captured at .planning/todos/pending/2026-06-17-shared-folder-move-must-reencrypt-file-metadata.md).

BinEntry legacy entries (without originalFolderKeyEncrypted) falling back to folderTree: if a file is deleted AND its original parent folder is also deleted before restore, the file is stuck until the parent is restored first — the legacy fallback cannot re-encrypt without the source key.
Desktop e2e move-content test added to test-cross-client-sync.sh but can only run in CI FUSE environment — not locally verifiable.
Literal raw-bytea Postgres read for at-rest ciphertext verification is out of web-e2e harness reach; the GET /shares/sent hex-not-equal-plaintext check is used as a proxy instead.

Phase 47 summaries backfilled post-hoc, but no process fix was applied to prevent shipping phases without SUMMARY.md files in future — the GSD planning loop will continue to false-positive on any similar gap.
PR #505 verification checklist's two-party live UAT item was updated to 'covered by share-itemname-backfill.spec.ts' but the raw-bytea at-rest assertion remains unchecked.

The transcript ends with the bin-restore robust fix committed but the debug session document and remaining task commits (desktop test, todo file) appear to be in progress — the final commit grouping was not confirmed.
